FW_A.name: Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT)
mandatory_elements: Exact Article Title as root heading
Clinical Bottom Line: Direct interpretive takeaway synthesizing therapeutic efficacy, safety profile, and methodological validity caveats

Results in Context: Primary outcome with point estimates, HR/RR, 95% CIs, p-values; absolute risk reduction (ARR) and NNT; primary and disease-specific secondary/surrogate endpoints with validated clinical criteria (e.g. RECIST/iRECIST in oncology, MACE in cardiology, eGFR slope in nephrology, EDSS in neurology, HbA1c in diabetology); patient-reported outcomes (PROs) with anchor-based MID thresholds; key adverse events drawing from CONSORT Harms 2022

Assertive Critical Appraisal: RoB 2 overall judgment (Low / Some concerns / High) across all 5 domains; subgroup credibility audit; composite endpoint deconstruction; CONSORT reporting quality (allocation concealment, flow diagram)
Research Objective: Explicit trial hypothesis, primary and secondary research questions
Study Design: Trial design (parallel-group, multi-arm, crossover, factorial, adaptive), randomization methodology, blinding of participants/personnel/assessors
Setting and Participants: Participant count, recruitment period, setting/centers, inclusion and exclusion criteria
Bibliographic Data: Title, Authors, Journal, Year, DOI / PubMed ID
negative_constraints: NO medical disclaimers
NO conversational pleasantries or filler phrases
NO therapeutic mandates beyond what the study evaluated
Ground EVERY factual claim with an inline coordinate anchor (e.g. [Methods, Para 3], [Results, Table 2])
Cite the matching rule ID (e.g. {R_ROB2_D1_RANDOMIZATION}) for every critical appraisal point

FW_B.name: Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis
mandatory_elements: Clinical Bottom Line: Direct interpretive summary integrating pooled effect estimates with evidence certainty
Results in Context: Summary of pooled results with exact effect sizes (OR/RR/HR) and 95% CIs; brief definition of statistical terms used; participant and included study counts

Assertive Critical Appraisal: GRADE certainty ratings (High/Moderate/Low/Very Low) per critical outcome with downgrade reasons; Higgins I^2 heterogeneity magnitude and Cochran Q; publication bias assessment (funnel plot / Egger test); special consideration if overall pooled result is significant but individual studies are not; PRISMA reporting quality audit (flow diagram, search strategy)
Research Objective: PICO question (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes)
Study Design: Systematic review protocol registration, databases searched, search date range, pooling model (random vs fixed effects)
Setting and Participants: Included trial settings, total pooled participant count, inclusion and exclusion criteria
Bibliographic Data: Title, Authors, Journal, Year, DOI
negative_constraints: NO medical disclaimers
NO conversational filler
Ground EVERY factual claim with an inline coordinate anchor
Cite the matching rule ID for every critical appraisal point

FW_C.name: Observational Study / Real-World Evidence
mandatory_elements: Clinical Bottom Line: Interpretive summary of observed associations, explicitly emphasizing that observational studies cannot prove causation due to residual confounding and bias

Results in Context: Main unadjusted and confounder-adjusted estimates (Odds Ratios, Relative Risks, Hazard Ratios) with 95% CIs for all key exposures/biomarkers; definitions of statistical metrics used; participant counts across follow-up stages

Assertive Critical Appraisal: STROBE bias critique (residual lifestyle confounding, reverse causality, survival selection, immortal time bias); STROBE confounding adjustment evaluation; RECORD assessment for routine health data / registry linkage (data provenance, ICD diagnostic coding, attrition); generalizability / clinical applicability
Research Objective: Specific observational objectives, exposure-outcome hypotheses
Study Design: Design type (prospective/retrospective cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), follow-up duration, statistical adjustment methods
Setting and Participants: Setting, location, data collection dates, registry sources, participant eligibility and selection criteria
Bibliographic Data: Title, Authors, Journal, Year, DOI
negative_constraints: NO medical disclaimers
NO conversational filler
Ground EVERY factual claim with an inline coordinate anchor
Cite the matching rule ID for every critical appraisal point

FW_D.name: Diagnostic Accuracy Study
mandatory_elements: Clinical Bottom Line: Definitive assessment of diagnostic utility, clinical applicability, and test safety

Results in Context: Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values (PPV/NPV), positive and negative likelihood ratios (LR+/LR-), and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC/ROC) with 95% CIs; 2x2 contingency table cross-tabulation

Assertive Critical Appraisal: STARD 2015 adherence; gold reference standard validity and independence; blinding between index test and reference standard interpreters; verification bias (partial work-up bias); spectrum bias / case-mix representativeness
Research Objective: Stated clinical role of the index test (triage, screening, replacement, add-on)
Study Design: Prospective vs retrospective diagnostic design, consecutive vs convenience sampling, timing of index test and reference standard
Setting and Participants: Clinical setting (primary, secondary, emergency), patient presenting symptoms, inclusion and exclusion criteria
Bibliographic Data: Title, Authors, Journal, Year, DOI

FW_E.name: Clinical Trial Protocol & Statistical Analysis Plan
mandatory_elements: Clinical Bottom Line: Methodological summary of the trial protocol, evaluating feasibility, ethical integrity, and potential design pitfalls prior to trial completion
Results in Context: Planned outcome metrics, targeted effect size, projected sample size, statistical power (1-beta), and alpha thresholds; anticipated timeline and milestones

Assertive Critical Appraisal: SPIRIT 2013 checklist adherence; sample size calculation assumptions audit; statistical analysis plan (SAP) pre-specification (primary models, missing data strategies); interim analysis and stopping rules for efficacy, futility, or safety harms; DSMB governance
Research Objective: Primary and secondary research questions, trial hypotheses
Study Design: Allocation ratio, blinding mechanisms, intervention and comparator dosing schedules, master protocol / adaptive design features
Setting and Participants: Target enrollment count, participating trial centers, inclusion and exclusion criteria
Bibliographic Data: Title, Authors, Journal, Year, Protocol Version, ClinicalTrials.gov ID

FW_F.name: Non-Inferiority Randomized Controlled Trial
mandatory_elements: Clinical Bottom Line: Direct verdict on whether non-inferiority was conclusively demonstrated, secondary superiority claims, and safety trade-offs

Results in Context: Point estimates and two-sided 95% (or 90%) confidence intervals compared against the pre-specified delta margin for both ITT and Per-Protocol (PP) populations; ARR, NNT, and harm metrics; disease-specific secondary and surrogate endpoints with validated clinical criteria (e.g. MACE, mortality, functional scores)

Assertive Critical Appraisal: Dual ITT and Per-Protocol analysis concordance audit (challenging non-inferiority if PP fails or is omitted); strategic trial objective audit (replacement trial promising safety/convenience trade-offs vs pure alternative option trial); statistical and clinical justification of Delta margin (preserving >= 50% active control historical efficacy); assay sensitivity and constancy assumption evaluation; biocreep risk; RoB 2 appraisal
Research Objective: Non-inferiority hypothesis and active comparator rationale
Study Design: Parallel-group active-controlled design, blinding, pre-specified delta margin
Setting and Participants: Participant counts across ITT and PP sets, trial centers, eligibility criteria
Bibliographic Data: Title, Authors, Journal, Year, DOI

FW_G.name: Health Economic Evaluation
mandatory_elements: Clinical Bottom Line: Clear statement of cost-effectiveness or budget impact relative to standard willingness-to-pay thresholds

Results in Context: Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) or incremental cost-utility ratio (ICUR) per QALY/DALY; total incremental costs and incremental health outcomes; cost currency and reference price year

Assertive Critical Appraisal: CHEERS 2022 compliance; time horizon and discount rate rationale audit; presence of a priori Health Economic Analysis Plan (HEAP); distributional cost-effectiveness and equity impacts across subgroups; patient and public involvement (PPIE); decision model structural assumptions; deterministic sensitivity analysis (tornado diagrams) and probabilistic sensitivity analysis (PSA / CEAC curves); health state utility valuation methods
Research Objective: Economic evaluation perspective (societal, healthcare payer) and target policy question
Study Design: Model type (Markov cohort, decision tree, microsimulation, trial-based CEA), cycle length, time horizon
Setting and Participants: Target patient cohort, clinical setting, jurisdiction / healthcare system context

Results in Context: Synthesis of key clinical concepts, physiological mechanisms, or therapeutic summaries presented with cited evidentiary support

Study Design: Non-systematic literature overview / expert commentary framework

FW_I.name: Biomarker & Genomic Medicine Study
mandatory_elements: Clinical Bottom Line: Direct summary of biomarker prognostic or predictive validity and potential clinical utility in patient management

Results in Context: Point estimates, Hazard Ratios (HR), Odds Ratios (OR), or AUC with 95% CIs across biomarker strata; assay Limit of Detection (LOD), Variant Allele Fraction (VAF%), or biomarker concentration ranges

Assertive Critical Appraisal: REMARK guideline adherence; pre-analytical biospecimen handling and assay reproducibility; cut-point pre-specification audit (flagging data-driven optimal cutpoints without holdout validation); multivariable survival models demonstrating independent prognostic value beyond standard clinical staging; distinction between prognostic vs predictive biomarker roles (requiring interaction tests); for ctDNA, exclusion of CHIP mutations
Research Objective: Biomarker biological rationale, prospective vs retrospective validation question

Study Design: Cohort or embedded trial design, biospecimen sampling timeline, analytical platform (NGS, PCR, IHC), and ctDNA assay classification: explicitly specify whether the assay is tumor-informed (patient-specific, personalized variant tracking) or tumor-naïve (fixed panel hotspot tracking), noting implications for analytical sensitivity and MRD false-negative rates
Setting and Participants: Patient cohort size, specimen repository source, clinical stages, inclusion and exclusion criteria
Bibliographic Data: Title, Authors, Journal, Year, DOI
negative_constraints: NO medical disclaimers
NO conversational filler

FW_J.name: Survey Research
mandatory_elements: Clinical Bottom Line: Direct summary of survey findings, attitudes, or organizational practices with caveats regarding sampling and generalizability
Results in Context: Summary of survey responses with frequency counts, percentages, Likert scale distributions, and 95% CIs; comparative analyses between respondent subgroups

Assertive Critical Appraisal: Good Practice in Survey Research (Kelley et al.) adherence; sampling frame coverage and representativeness; response rate calculation and non-response bias assessment (early vs late responders); questionnaire instrument validity, cognitive pre-testing, and pilot testing; neutral question framing
Research Objective: Survey aims, research questions, target constructs measured
Study Design: Survey methodology (web-based, postal, telephone, interview), questionnaire structure, distribution strategy
Setting and Participants: Target population, sample size, eligible respondents, geographic or clinical setting
